To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the finite- temperature confinement phase transition in a gauge theory is a long-distance phenomenon in the order parameter, and that the critical properties of this transition are universal.

the critical behavior of confinement phase transitions at finite temperature is described by the renormalization-group fixed points of the effective scalar field theory, and that the critical exponents depend on the dimensionality of space-time and the center symmetry group of the gauge theory, and not on any details of the gauge theory.

(a) confinement transitions in pure gauge theories at non-zero temperature can be discussed in terms an order parameter that transforms under a global center symmetry, (b) the effective theory for this order parameter has only short-range coupliings, and hence that (c) the confinement transition is accompanied by only long-range fluctuations in the order parameter, and (d) universality ideas then lead, in conjunction with the short-range effective theory, to the prediction of the critical behavior at the transition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the critical phenomena associated with confinement transitions in gauge theories.
the critical behavior of a class of systems which exhibit confinement transitions in the presence of a global symmetry group.
the critical behavior of the finite-temperature confining phase transition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the critical behavior of a pure gauge theory is that of the order parameter field, and that the critical exponents are independent of the underlying gauge theory.
there is no evidence for a non-trivial infrared fixed point in the effective action for the order parameter.
the finite- T confinement transition is in the same universality class as the zero- T confinement transition.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the order-parameter field theory has a very simple form and can be solved exactly.
the critical exponents for the confinement phase transition in a pure gauge field theory are universal and independent of the details of the gauge group and the number of space-time dimensions.
